structured_content.summary:
Implementation: `RepoTools::call_many_until` delegates batched calls to `execute_tools_until`, which starts up to `concurrency` sibling futures in a `FuturesUnordered`, records each start time, awaits whichever completes, and stores results by input index—preserving order. Per-tool timeout produces a failed result with elapsed duration; ordinary `call_one` success/failure paths also attach duration metadata. [lib.rs](crates/repo-tools/src/lib.rs:70) [exec.rs](crates/repo-tools/src/exec.rs:52)

On deadline expiry, the select returns immediately, `in_flight.clear()` drops outstanding futures, and missing entries receive synthesized failed “batch deadline expired” results with elapsed duration (or zero if never started). Grep subprocesses use `kill_on_drop(true)`, so cancellation relies on dropping the future/child to terminate them. [exec.rs](crates/repo-tools/src/exec.rs:101) [grep.rs](crates/repo-tools/src/grep.rs:142)

The regression change surface is therefore `crates/repo-tools/src/exec.rs`: after the deadline fires, non-ready futures must be polled/drained so siblings that completed concurrently are collected before cancellation; then synthesize metadata only for genuinely outstanding calls. Keep subprocess cleanup in `grep.rs` (and verify cancellation remains effective). The focused test already asserts completed-result retention, sibling cancellation, failure status, and duration behavior. [exec.rs](crates/repo-tools/src/exec.rs:246)

- Drains already-ready sibling results before canceling remaining futures.
- Cancels pending work and ensures `rg` subprocesses use kill-on-drop.
- Produces consistent failure and elapsed-duration metadata.
- Carries one absolute deadline through model and repository-tool calls.
- Added regression coverage for results completing in the same scheduler turn as the deadline.
